Which unit the number is (digits vs width) still cannot be proven.

name: Ui_ListRow_DrawEquipComparisonTwoHand
signature: void Ui_ListRow_DrawEquipComparisonTwoHand(void* row, u32 memberIndex, u16* itemEntry, u32 stack)
summary: Equip-comparison row renderer for two-handed items: returns unless 0x0066C5CC classifies the item as 2H (equip category 5..9), otherwise builds the member stat context (Party_StatCalc_SetupMemberContext), formats the item (0x0045A5A0 with mode 0), recomputes the stats and tail-dispatches through g_uiListRowDrawDispatchFuncs[row+4].
evidence: NEW: FACTS.md confirms 0x0066C5CC is the two-handed equip-category check while 0x0066C5A8 is the one-handed one; this function tests only 0x0066C5CC, which is what separates it from the two 1H variants, so the A/B/C suffix is replaced by the real filter. The stat-context callees are now named as well.

name: Ui_ListRow_DrawEquipComparisonOneHandFiltered
signature: void Ui_ListRow_DrawEquipComparisonOneHandFiltered(void* row, u32 memberIndex, u16* itemEntry, u32 stack)
summary: Equip-comparison row renderer for one-handed items with a category filter: requires 0x0066C5A8 to accept the item as 1H, skips when the item's equip category (ItemRecord+0x29) differs from the row filter byte at row+5 (0xFF = any), then builds the member stat context, formats the item with mode 0 and tail-dispatches through g_uiListRowDrawDispatchFuncs[row+4].
evidence: NEW: FACTS.md identifies 0x0066C5A8 as the 1H (category 0..4) check and 0x0066C5CC as 2H, so 0x006511E0 / 0x006526D0 / 0x00652798 are the 2H and 1H halves of one comparison renderer rather than arbitrary A/B/C twins; the +0x29 vs row+5 test is a per-row equip-category filter.

name: Ui_ListRow_DrawEquipComparisonOneHandBest
signature: void Ui_ListRow_DrawEquipComparisonOneHandBest(void* row, u32 memberIndex, u16* itemEntry, u32 stack)
summary: Same 1H + equip-category-filter renderer as 0x006526D0, but it formats the item with mode 1 and tail-dispatches through g_uiEquipBestItemScoreFuncs[row+4]: the 'best item' scoring variant of the equip-comparison row.
evidence: NEW: the only differences from 0x006526D0 are the format mode (1 instead of 0) and the dispatch table (g_uiEquipBestItemScoreFuncs instead of g_uiListRowDrawDispatchFuncs), and its one caller is a UI context allocator, so this is the variant installed for best-item scoring.

evidence: NEW: the callees are now named (Battle_BuildTargetSlotsForCommand, Member_RemoveItemAtSlot neighbours) and the body is a single guarded apply step, so 'confirm selection' became the more accurate 'apply the selection to the member'; the panel class and the meaning of the 0x12E0 pair are still unknown.

evidence: NEW: the callee 0x0066B088 is now read as a per-id state test on the save bag and both callers of the twin are known to be icon-placement code, but no caller names this instance's screen, so the A/B names stay.

evidence: NEW: the mask source is now identified as a bag bitmask keyed by the object's own save key (0x0066B64C), so this builds one pane per row of a saved list and greys out the unused ones; 'ChildTransform' described the wrong thing.

name: maybe_Battle_Action_TestFlag80OrMemberHandFlag
signature: u8 maybe_Battle_Action_TestFlag80OrMemberHandFlag(void* unit, int hand, u8* action)
summary: For a party unit with action[0x10] set: resolves the action's skill (+0xFF) or spell (+0x2E8) record and returns 1 when bit 0x80 is set; otherwise falls back to the acting member's per-hand byte at +0xDED / +0xDEE. Non-party units just get action[0x10] back.

evidence: NEW: the callee list is now fully named (std_wcsncpy, std_wcsncat, Str_WcsStr, Ui_SpriteSpan_Select, Ui_Pane_PlayLayoutAnim, Game_GetDisplayModeFlag), which matches a text+sprite detail page; the body itself is cut off right after a mis-marked-noreturn wcslen, so the MonsterBook owner is still inferred from the callee set only.

evidence: NEW: the entry-flag comparison against work+index*0x10+0x2A260 is visible in the recovered body, so the 'pick first enabled entry' reading replaces the unsupported 'UmaWindow page select'; the body still carries heritage warnings and dead-code removal, so the confidence stays at 0.3.

signature: u8 maybe_Data_GetRowKind(void* model, u32 rowIndex, u32 unusedArg3, u32 workOut)

evidence: NEW: the callers are now named (Ui_SakusenWindow_PushCommandForCursor, Ui_SakusenWindow_UpdateDetailList, maybe_Ui_Window_ResetChildrenF), which supports the free-slot query reading; the callee and the table it scans are still unnamed, and the value is used without being returned here.

name: maybe_Script_ResolveNameHandle
summary: Validates a name-table id through the data manager, rolls a 0..99 draw and, when the record's probability byte accepts it, builds the random name variant (std_ConstructArray over Math_WeightedRandomIndexDefaultRng); finally writes the 3-word tagged handle with tag 2.

Only caller is Battle_ActionModel_UpdateUnitVisibility.

name: maybe_Field_ActorMove_Finish

The twin 0x001E10F4 sends code 0 and applies the pending offsets instead.

name: maybe_Field_ActorMove_ApplyStep
summary: Re-sends the placement request for task->targetActor with code 0 (0x00642280, also for the matching object in the UI object list) and then adds the task's two pending offsets (animNameWord0/Word1) to the actor's +0xC4 and +0xC8 - the per-frame movement step.
evidence: NEW: the body's tail adds the task words into actor+0xC4/+0xC8, which is the actual move application; its twin 0x001E0D44 clears isMoving and plays idle. So 'Register' described only the first half and the pair names were swapped.

name: Ui_NotifyList_BuildEntries
summary: Fills the notification list: one type-0xE1 entry per non-empty row of the bag table at work+0x24A98 (count 0x0066B820, entry 0x0066B5E8), plus type-0xE5 entries from the 90 slots whose type byte is 7, then sorts everything with std_List_MergeSort.

name: maybe_Field_Npc_StartIdleForScript

name: maybe_Battle_GetWeaponActionRow

summary: Refreshes and returns the unit's MP display pair: converts member +0x744, +0xEC4 and +0xB04 to float, marks the layout dirty when the enemy slot's value changed, and returns the (+0x744, +0xEC4) pair that the caller turns into a bar ratio.

summary: Field actor per-frame update: reads the scene node position, sets up the camera projection from the actor's +0x12 transform and runs Field_NpcUpdateMoveAnimation when the actor's checks pass. The prologue is damaged (unaff_r4/unaff_r6), so the argument list is not real.

name: maybe_MenuCondition_RequiredItemsMet
signature: u32 maybe_MenuCondition_RequiredItemsMet(u32 self, RecipeRow* conditionRow, u32 arg3, u32 work)
summary: Evaluates a menu-condition row: when the selector byte +0x1A is -1 each non-empty material id (+0x11, +0x12, +0x14, +0x16, +0x18) must be present via Item_CountEquipped; otherwise Party_ResolveAppearanceVariantIndex(+0x11) must equal +0x1A. The decompiled success path returns 0, so the polarity is not trustworthy.
evidence: NEW: the callers are now named (Ui_UmaWindow_HandlePageInput/ApplyPurchase/SetOddsRow, Model_FindEntryById) and the neighbouring Item_CountEquipped/Party_ResolveAppearanceVariantIndex identify this as a menu-condition evaluator, not a plain item query; the inverted return on the success path means the truth value stays in doubt.

name: maybe_Field_ResolveNpcBalloonKind
signature: BalloonEntry* maybe_Field_ResolveNpcBalloonKind(u32 table, u32 field, u32 arg3, u32 scratch)
summary: Looks a placement record up in the work entry table (work+8 -> +0xB4), maps the entry's per-id state byte (0x0066AF08 on the bag) to a balloon type (1 -> 3, 2 -> 6, 3 -> ...), and falls back to the placement record's own +0x14 pointer when the state is unknown.
evidence: NEW: the state mapping through the bag per-id getter and the +0x14 fallback are now readable, so this resolves which balloon an NPC shows; the argument order is still unverified because the original Thumb body uses unaff_r6.

name: Ui_Overlay_GetCursorRowState
summary: Hit-tests the list under the cursor and dispatches on the picked component's class chain: equipment rows return a weapon-type code (Ui_Equipment_GetWeaponTypeA), bag rows return 0 or 3 (Ui_BagList_GetRowState), and other classes fall through to 0.
evidence: NEW: both leaf callees and the class tests are now named, and the caller (maybe_Menu_ApplyRowColorState) maps the result to colour commands, so this is the cursor row's state/colour class; the mixed kind/state return value is documented in the summary.

name: maybe_Item_BuildModelPath
signature: void* maybe_Item_BuildModelPath(u16* key, void* group, unsigned int arg3, unsigned int manager)
summary: Resolves the entry at key+8 through its relative link chain, re-resolves the id through the data manager's item table (0x0063CDD8) when the chain is broken, then formats the shared item-model path buffer with g_resPathUiItemBch and returns it.
evidence: NEW: the named callers (Ui_Pane_CreateEffectForItemId, Gfx_EffectObject_Replace, Ui_Window_RefreshEffect) all need an item's model path, and the body ends in the shared g_itemModelPathBuffer / g_resPathUiItemBch formatting, so the item-model path reading replaces the vague 'resolve relative entry' wording.

name: Snd_InitStreamContext
summary: Initialises a 24-channel sound context under the monitor lock: opens the kernel handle, tags it with unit flag bit 2, queries the unit count, stores the 0x2000-byte transfer buffer size, resets the channel objects and returns 0 or a Horizon error (0xC8A0A801 when the query fails).
evidence: NEW: the callees are now named (Snd_InvalidateChannelObjects, Snd_ResetChannelUnitsInPlace, Snd_RestoreChannelState, Os_Lock/UnlockMonitor) and the SVc_Ndm_AcquireService call in the same block shows the streaming/NDM context; no caller exists but the whole body is a single init sequence.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelLevel
summary: Stores a u16 at channel block +0xBC and sets dirty bit 0x10000 on the block's flag word; called from Snd_InitChannelState and Snd_RestoreChannelState, so it publishes/replays a saved channel field.
evidence: NEW: the init/restore caller pair places this in the saved DSP channel state, and the per-field dirty bits confirm each setter owns one field; which field +0xBC is (level vs something else) still rests on the default value only, so the name keeps its maybe_ prefix.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelFormat
summary: Stores a u16 at channel block +0x18 and sets dirty bit 0x8000000; published by Snd_InitChannelState and replayed by Snd_RestoreChannelState.
evidence: NEW: the same init/restore pair as the other channel setters; the +0x18 field and the dirty bit are certain, the 'format' meaning is still an inference from the value Snd_InitChannelState publishes, so the maybe_ prefix stays.

name: Snd_SetChannelGain
summary: Stores a float at channel block +0x04 and sets dirty bit 0x10000. Snd_InitChannelState publishes 1.0f into this field and Snd_RestoreChannelState replays it, which is what makes it a gain-like scalar.
evidence: NEW: the three callers are now named (Snd_InitChannelState, Snd_RestoreChannelState, Sound_Channel_SetDecodeHook) and the published default is 1.0f for a float field - the same pattern the named SetUnitGain has; the float store itself is a VFP s0 argument Ghidra shows only as in_s0.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelAdpcmState
signature: u32 maybe_Snd_SetChannelAdpcmState(ChannelBuffer* channelBuffer, int unit, u16 value)
summary: Stores a u16 in the per-unit halfword at channel+0x24+unit*2 and sets dirty bit 0x40 (unit 0) or 0x80 (unit 1); replayed per unit by Snd_RestoreChannelState.
evidence: NEW: the per-unit shape (two slots, two dirty bits) is confirmed by the restore path, but nothing in the named callers says the two halfwords are ADPCM state rather than, say, loop points or sample indices; keeps its maybe_ prefix.

name: Snd_SetUnitGain
signature: void Snd_SetUnitGain(ChannelBuffer* channelBuffer, int unit, float value)
summary: Stores a float in the per-unit field at channel+0x08+unit*4 and sets dirty bit 0x1000000 (unit 0) or 0x2000000 (unit 1). Snd_InitChannelState publishes 1.0f for both units, so these are per-unit gain scalars.
evidence: NEW: three named callers (Snd_InitChannelState, Snd_RestoreChannelState, Sound_Channel_InvokeCallback) plus the 1.0f default for a float field and the dedicated per-unit dirty bits; the float arrives in VFP s0, which Ghidra renders as in_s0, hence the explicit phrasing.

name: Snd_SetChannelVolume
summary: Stores a u16 in the channel block's field at +0x10 and sets dirty bit 0x8000. Snd_InitChannelState publishes 2 here, Snd_RestoreChannelState replays the saved state word, and Snd_SetOutputMode also writes it.
evidence: NEW: the three named callers (init, restore, Snd_SetOutputMode) confirm this is a saved channel-state field that the output-mode switch also touches; the default of 2 fits a volume/level field. The wording stays 'Volume' because the field offset and dirty bit are what is proven.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelOutput
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelOutput(ChannelBuffer* channelBuffer, unsigned int outputSelect)
summary: Writes a value below 2 into the channel's field at +0x1E and marks the block dirty with bit 0x40000000; returns 1 on write, 0 otherwise.
evidence: NEW: the only plausible caller is the restore-path branch at 0x00112D60 (the 13 other xrefs in the dossier land on a neighbouring shared helper), and the '< 2' guard plus the single two-valued field is the only argument for reading it as an output selector; that is not enough to drop the maybe_.

name: Gfx_CloseGpuSession
summary: Closes the GPU session: sends the 0x00020000 close command through Gfx_IpcCmd20000, closes the display-transfer shared memory and the gsp::Gpu service handle (svc 0x23), releases the remaining shared memory and clears the open flag.
evidence: NEW: the body uses only GPU globals (g_gpuSessionTimeout, g_displayTransferSharedMemory, g_gspGpuServiceHandle) and the named neighbours Gfx_IpcCmd20000 / Gfx_OpenGpuChannel / Gfx_ShutdownChannel, and its 16 callers are SDK shutdown paths - so this is the GPU session close. The first pass's 'ir:USER' justification does not match this body at all (that literal belongs to a different function).

name: maybe_Svc_SyncObject_DestroyB
summary: Destroys a synchronisation object: Os_CloseHandle on the stored handle, then svcCloseHandle (svc 0x23) on the second kernel handle and clears it; returns the object pointer.
evidence: NEW: the sibling 0x00509A20 has the same shape with a different close helper and both are waited on by the content-cache code, so the destroy role is supported; which two sync primitives are involved is still unknown, hence the maybe_ and the 'B' suffix.
